key_insight: Hard math prompts can jump from unsolved to solved, and higher early-generation entropy in failed attempts helps identify failures worth learning from.
engineering_relevance: RLVR training can use informative failed rollouts to provide learning signals when standard group-relative updates vanish on entirely unsolved groups.
method: Rank failed rollouts in unsolved groups with an early-branching driver.
Integrate NAPO with GRPO to assign graded advantages to those failures.
evidence_signal: Under fixed rollout budgets, NAPO accelerated early solution discovery and improved Pass@256 by 10.0 points on AIME24 and 6.6 points on AIME2025.
watch_item: The abstract reports math-benchmark gains but does not establish whether the negative-ranking signal generalizes to other tasks or model scales.
paper_title: What Drives the Zero-to-One Jump? Diagnosing and Steering Hard-Prompt Learning in RLVR
